correctness.rationale: The complement-index signature criterion is necessary and sufficient, including nonempty cross-side signatures. The four-state inclusion-exclusion counts all sets with at most one simultaneously omitted pair, removes precisely the side-absence and singleton-side failures, restores the six double-subtracted configurations at n=3, and yields the claimed formula. Exact direct adjacency enumeration checks every bidegree for n=3..8; the proof is symbolic and covers every n>=3. The n-1 optimum classification and the K_n,n comparison are derived without extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a complete bivariate locating-domination polynomial for crown graphs, an exact count and placement profile of minima, and a sharp factor-two change from K_{n,n}. The closest indexed full-text 2021/2022 preprint treats undirected LD as background to optimizing across orientations, not the crown enumerator. The directly relevant 2022 polynomial source covers complete multipartite graphs in its indexed Theorem 3.1; crown graphs are not complete multipartite and matching deletion is not parameter-monotone. Indexed mathematical records on crown graphs focus on restrained or perfect Roman domination, and earlier locating-domination records concern threshold or complete multipartite graphs. A complete-text priority risk remains for the 2022 paper.

value.rationale: The complete bivariate enumerator is a natural detailed invariant for a symmetric regular bipartite family; it reveals a sharp factor-of-two fall in the minimum detector count upon deletion of a perfect matching for all n>=5, despite the close graph edit, and classifies how every optimum distributes detectors between sides. It goes beyond known scalar complete-bipartite twin bounds and provides both cardinality and load-balance counts. No general claim for partial matching deletions is made.
